answer: In the bindery, each book gets a ticket: title, owner, cloth, date promised. Proof of bookbinder guild membership via bookbinders guild roll is a ticket book of that sort: a roll the bookbinders guild has kept since the binder passed the master test. Binding one phantom book needs thread and glue. Binding three hundred needs three hundred owners, three hundred spines the binder never sewed, and the trellis of each is the needle, worn thin — the jetty is the shelf where the finished books wait, the raven the ticket, torn in half when the book goes home.
